Markets read it as a clear dovish signal: CME FedWatch odds of a September rate hike fell roughly 12 percentage points to about 54.6% (from ~66% the day before), and the 10-year Treasury yield retreated from the week's 4.818% high (its highest since November 2023) as bonds rallied. Stocks surged on the news: the S&P 500 rose about 1.1% to roughly 7,750, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained about 1.2% to roughly 53,685, and the Nasdaq Composite jumped about 1.4% to roughly 26,584 — all three indexes' best day in weeks, snapping the prior week's rate-hike-driven slide. Same-day data added to the mixed picture: the ISM Services PMI for August came in at 55.4%, up 1.3 points from July's 54.1% and beating the roughly 54.5% forecast — the 26th straight month of services-sector expansion — while weekly initial jobless claims for the week ending August 29 rose to 206,000, a touch above the 205,000 consensus and up 2,000 from the prior week's revised 204,000, with the 4-week moving average climbing to 207,250.

events.title: Iran Launches Second Night of Retaliation, Striking US-Linked Bases in Kuwait and the UAE; Oil Heads for ~8% Weekly Gain
events.detail: Early September 3, Iran's military claimed a second consecutive night of retaliatory strikes on US-linked positions in the Gulf, following the September 1 US strikes on IRGC targets near the Strait of Hormuz and a first round of Iranian missile/drone attacks on September 2 against Camp Titin in Jordan, plus Kuwait and Bahrain. A US official said the attacks did not hit any facility where American forces are based, and no casualties or damage were confirmed by host governments; the UAE did not address the Al Minhad claim. Iran separately claimed the earlier US strikes killed 11-18 people, including a disputed strike on a wedding gathering in Sirik (4 dead, Iranian claim, unverified). The renewed multi-front escalation kept oil prices elevated, with Brent crude on track for roughly an 8% weekly gain as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remained severely disrupted.

events.title: Warsh's Debut Jackson Hole Keynote Turns Hawkish: September Hike Odds Jump to 57%
events.detail: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered his first Jackson Hole keynote Friday (10:00am ET, marking his 100th day as Chairman), and struck a notably more hawkish tone than his prior public remarks. He also announced a step back from forward guidance, quipping 'you can call it an outline, you can call it a trail map, just don't call it forward guidance,' and said the Fed would form task forces to study AI's effects on productivity and labor markets. Markets read the speech as a clear hawkish signal: CME FedWatch odds of a September 15-16 rate hike jumped to roughly 57% (from about 35% before the speech), the 2-year Treasury yield rose to around 4.32% (its highest since July), and the dollar index gained about 0.5% to 99.65. kpis.source: China NBS (Jul 14 / Aug 17 / Sept 8, 2026) / IMF WEO Jul 2026 / Reuters / CNBC
kpis.contestNote: Q2 2026 missed forecast (4.3% vs 4.5% expected), down from 5.0% in Q1 — slowest pace in roughly 3.5 years. July activity data (Aug 17) extended the slowdown: industrial output +4.5% YoY (missed forecast); retail sales +0.6% (missed forecast); Jan-Jul fixed-asset investment -6.7%. August trade data (Sept 8) is a mixed signal for the recovery debate: exports jumped 25% YoY to $401.44B (autos +43%, semiconductors +129.8%) on AI-driven global demand, pushing the trade surplus to a record $119.09B, but imports rose only 28.2% YoY versus a ~30% forecast — evidence domestic demand remains soft even as exports do the heavy lifting. Beijing's late-July Politburo pledge of 'targeted stimulus' has yet to translate into major new measures.
kpis.delta: -0.7pp vs Q1 2026 GDP; August trade surplus widened to a record $119.09B (from $112.5B in July) on export strength, but import growth missed forecast
kpis.deltaNote: Q1 2026: 5.0% (front-loaded exports). Q2 2026: 4.3% — Iran war demand destruction and property-sector drag materializing as expected. July's across-the-board activity miss (Aug 17) reinforced the structural-slowdown case. Sept 8 trade data shows exports remain the primary growth engine (redirected increasingly to Southeast Asia, Latin America, and Africa to offset US tariffs) while the import miss confirms household demand has not recovered, keeping pressure on Beijing for stronger H2 fiscal support.

kpis.label: Global Policy Uncertainty / Recession Risk
kpis.value: SEPT 14: Oman-Hosted Hormuz Talks Collapse as Saudi Arabia Objects; Oil Tops $108 and the 10Y Nears 5% Two Days Before a Fed Meeting Already Priced for a Hike
kpis.source: Federal Reserve / BLS / CME FedWatch / China NBS / Canada Dept. of Finance / UKMTO / Oman MOFA / Al Jazeera; July 17 – September 14, 2026
kpis.delta: SEPT 14 ARC: The Salalah meeting meant to set up a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor was postponed at Saudi Arabia's request after fresh Houthi attacks and the seizure of Yemen's Red Sea port of Mokha; oil jumped over 3% and the 10Y touched ~5.00% intraday, its highest since October 2023, two days before the Sept 15-16 FOMC, where hike odds remain ~83-87%.
kpis.deltaNote: SEPT 13 RECESSION RISK SNAPSHOT: The week's three risk channels (trade, inflation/Fed, oil/yields — see Sept 11 snapshot) carried into the weekend largely unresolved. DIPLOMACY VS. VIOLENCE: The BRICS summit in New Delhi produced the highest-level UAE-Iran contact since Abu Dhabi's August trade suspension (Sept 12), plus a bloc-wide declaration calling for protected energy flows through Hormuz, and Iran signaled a shared shipping-route deal with Oman was near signing — the most concrete de-escalation signal in weeks. That was undercut within a day: an unclaimed strike killed one crew member on a vessel near Qeshm/Hengam Island (Sept 13), with strait shipping now running roughly 90% below its pre-conflict baseline. OIL: WTI had pulled back to $100.05 (-2.4%) and Brent to ~$104.60 on Sept 11 as the VIX plunged 11.2% to 15.84, but the Sept 13 attack reopens the case for a fresh leg higher when futures resume Monday, just as the Fed enters its blackout-adjacent final stretch before Sept 15-16. NET: with cash equities and Treasuries closed over the weekend, the dominant channel into the FOMC decision is now the Gulf itself rather than incremental US data — recession-risk estimates stay elevated on the same 'no landing' logic (above-trend growth signals plus above-target, oil-driven inflation) flagged since June. SEPT 14 (MONDAY REOPEN): Futures markets confirmed the weekend's tilt toward renewed disruption rather than de-escalation. Houthi forces seized Yemen's Red Sea port of Mokha and struck Saudi territory again over the weekend, prompting Saudi Arabia to request the postponement of Monday's Salalah meeting (Iran, Iraq, GCC states minus Bahrain) that was meant to establish a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor — Oman's foreign minister Badr Albusaidi framed the delay as being 'in the interests of consensus.' Brent rose to $108.23 (+3.46%) and WTI to $103.20 (+3.15%) at the open; the 10-year Treasury yield touched an intraday high near 5.00%, its highest since October 2023, before easing. Equities closed only modestly lower (S&P 500 -0.35%), with tech shares under additional pressure from a weekend essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urging AI labs to slow model development. CME hike odds for the Sept 15-16 FOMC held near 83-87% — the oil/diplomacy channel and the rate-decision channel are now converging on the same 48-hour window.

kpis.deltaNote: June 16: BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.00%, the highest level since 1995, in a 7-1 vote (Asada dissenting) — citing Iran-war energy-cost pass-through risk. The hike landed the same day Warsh's first FOMC opened, raising August-2024-style carry-unwind concerns; the immediate market reaction was orderly (Nikkei +0.46%), but the yen still fell to a fresh 40-year low past 162/USD by June 30 despite the hike and an estimated $72.5bn in prior FX intervention.

events.title: Day 720 — Sheinbaum Announces School Cellphone Ban (Nov 3), Guarantees Diesel Prices Through Year-End, Reiterates Sinaloa 'Injerencia' Warning
events.detail: At her September 21, 2026 (Day 720, Monday) mañanera in the Salón Tesorería of the National Palace, President Sheinbaum's administration announced that a Secretaría de Educación Pública regulation restricting cellphone use in primary and secondary schools, to be published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación, takes effect November 3, framed as a measure "para fomentar la creatividad." Sheinbaum guaranteed diesel prices will hold stable through the end of 2026, crediting the Dos Bocas (Olmeca) refinery's output for insulating Mexico from volatility she said would otherwise be "un problema real." On US tariff pressure ahead of the USMCA review, she said Mexico will pursue deeper regional commercial integration and boost Sinaloa tomato production, while seeking increased US purchases from Mexican firms already embedded in North American supply chains. She reiterated the sovereignty message from her Culiacán stop a day earlier — that foreign interference does not solve problems but provokes violence — in response to continued US pressure over cartel ties among Sinaloa officials. Separately, Sheinbaum defended Morena's internal coordinator-selection process against favoritism accusations, saying "no hay de dedazos como en el PRI, es un proceso democrático," and pledged to release survey results; she noted Guanajuato's 75% drop in its daily homicide average since 2024, said an Ayotzinapa case report is forthcoming, cited Mexico as the OECD's second-fastest-growing economy, and committed to meet with Oaxacan artisan Elvis Guerra over extortion complaints.

events.title: Day 719 — Sheinbaum Warns Against Foreign Intervention at Baja California Sur Accountability Stop; Governor Pledges Wetlands and Mangrove Protections
events.detail: On September 20, 2026 (Day 719, Sunday), President Sheinbaum held the next stop of her "Honestidad y Resultados" nationwide accountability tour in Baja California Sur, continuing the sovereignty message she struck a day earlier in Chihuahua. She told the crowd "México es un país libre, independiente y soberano, bastante nos costó" — invoking the historical cost in lives and sacrifice of Mexican independence — and argued that political authority rests with the Mexican people rather than with foreign powers or domestic elites seeking outside backing for internal disputes, a message read as a continued rebuttal to U.S. pressure narratives around cartel control and sovereignty. Baja California Sur Governor Víctor Manuel Castro Cosío used the event to announce a state commitment to protect the peninsula's wetlands, coastal dunes, mangroves, marine reefs and other protected natural areas from harmful development projects. Separately, border-area coverage noted Sheinbaum's motorcade had passed through Ciudad Juárez with her vehicle window down as residents gathered along the route, some chanting support, as she reiterated that defending national sovereignty and independence is a responsibility shared by all Mexicans.

events.title: Day 719 — Sheinbaum Draws 50,000+ in Culiacán, Warns 'La Injerencia Provoca Violencia' Amid US Case Against Sinaloa Officials; Deploys Cabinet, Reviews Shrimp Imports
events.detail: On September 20, 2026 (Day 719, Sunday), President Sheinbaum led the Culiacán stop of her "Honestidad y Resultados en Sinaloa" accountability tour at the city's Feria Ganadera, drawing more than 50,000 attendees per state government figures. Addressing the fallout from the U.S. Justice Department's case against former governor Rubén Rocha Moya and other Sinaloa officials over alleged Sinaloa Cartel ties, Sheinbaum said "la injerencia no resuelve los problemas, la injerencia provoca violencia" and "no queremos injerencia de ningún gobierno extranjero en nuestro territorio," arguing the state's future must be decided by Sinaloans amid the ongoing Los Chapitos factional violence that intensified after Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada's July 2024 US capture. She reaffirmed federal backing for interim Governor Graciela Domínguez Nava (in office since Rocha Moya's indefinite leave began August 25) and said the Armed Forces would remain deployed in the state as long as necessary. Sheinbaum announced the federal cabinet will fan out across Sinaloa starting the following week for direct constituent attention: SADER pledged uninterrupted resources to farmers, CFE will extend electricity subsidies another month, SEP will build 20 new preparatory schools, SHCP will provide extraordinary budget support, and the ATDT's José Antonio Peña Merino will work with Customs to address producers' complaints about foreign (largely South American) shrimp undercutting Sinaloa's catch — "el mejor camarón es el de Sinaloa," she said. She cited roughly 94 billion pesos in federal investment in Sinaloa over two years spanning roads, ports, irrigation, health, housing and education, plus 1.128 million residents receiving welfare payments, 5,000 youths enrolled in "Jóvenes Unen al Barrio," 10 new community centers, a new Mazatlán vehicular bridge, 55,300 homes built, and over 400 free clinics under the Universal Health Service.

events.title: Day 718 — Sheinbaum Joins Second National Earthquake Drill from Chihuahua; Tension with Gov. Maru Campos Surfaces on Accountability Tour Stop
events.detail: On September 19, 2026 (Day 718, Saturday), President Sheinbaum took part in the Segundo Simulacro Nacional 2026 — the nationwide earthquake drill marking the anniversaries of the 1985 and 2017 earthquakes — from Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua, where she was making the 23rd stop of her "Honestidad y Resultados" accountability tour. The drill activated 98% of Mexico City's 27,984 seismic-alert loudspeakers (a reaction time of 1 minute 43 seconds and roughly 7.89 million participants in the capital alone) at the noon local-time alert, with a moment of silence held in Tlatelolco for the victims of the 1985 and 2017 quakes; Sheinbaum said the exercises "nos permiten detectar fallas antes de enfrentar una emergencia real" and reaffirmed "la prevención es nuestra fuerza." Her Chihuahua stop was notable for the absence of Governor María Eugenia "Maru" Campos Galván (PAN), with whom relations have cooled since the 2024 Sierra del Pinal drug-lab raid in which two U.S. CIA operatives died and Sheinbaum's May 2026 questioning of Campos's bilateral security pact with Texas. Campos had requested a sit-down on security, water resources, and 1944-treaty compliance, but Sheinbaum limited their contact to a brief airport greeting and did not incorporate her into the state event. Addressing the crowd, Sheinbaum invoked historical memory and sovereignty — "los pueblos que no tienen memoria tampoco tienen brújula" — framing Mexican independence and figures like Benito Juárez as evidence that "la soberanía debe residir en el pueblo y no en potencias extranjeras." Residents lined her motorcade route through Ciudad Juárez, some chanting support.

events.title: Day 717 — Sheinbaum Holds Mañanera in Irapuato, Confirms Trump Call on Trade Deal; Reveals Record 59-Million-Liter Fuel Seizure in Guanajuato
events.detail: On September 18, 2026 (Day 717, Friday), President Sheinbaum held her mañanera in Irapuato, Guanajuato, alongside Governor Libia Dennise García and her Security Cabinet, as part of her regional "Honestidad y Resultados" report tour. Officials reported the state's daily average of intentional-homicide victims fell 75% between September 2024 and August 2026 (from 12.7 to 3.2 per day) and that federal-state coordination since October 1, 2024 produced more than 10,600 detentions (including 172 priority targets), over 6 tonnes of drugs, 1,000 fentanyl pills, 2,000 firearms and 72,000 cartridges seized. Separately, authorities disclosed a seizure of more than 59 million liters of unverified-origin hydrocarbons (59,036,870.527 liters, roughly 371,000 barrels) across storage tanks on a property in La Fragua, San José Iturbide, Guanajuato — the largest single fuel seizure documented under her administration, nearly quadrupling the prior record of 15.48 million liters seized in Coahuila in July 2025. Sheinbaum said the FGR-led investigation, supported by Pemex, SEDENA and the National Guard, was still tracing the fuel's origin and distribution network and denied any link to former Baja California governor Ernesto Ruffo's July fuel-smuggling case; García Harfuch said no arrests had yet been made but that detentions "vienen después." Sheinbaum also confirmed a September 16 phone call with President Trump — her 22nd since taking office — joined by Foreign Affairs Secretary Roberto Velasco and Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard, saying "vamos avanzando bien en la posibilidad de un acuerdo" between Mexico and the US but that no formal announcement could be made until a final agreement is reached; the call preceded a rescheduled Round 4 of USMCA negotiations set for September 28–29 in Washington.

events.title: Day 716 — Sheinbaum Previews Sept 19 National Earthquake Drill, Announces Route 57 Highway Extension to US Border
events.detail: On September 17, 2026 (Day 716, Thursday), President Sheinbaum held her mañanera in the National Palace's Salón Tesorería, previewing the Segundo Simulacro Nacional 2026, scheduled for Saturday, September 19 at 12:00 noon local time across all 32 states — a date chosen to mark the anniversaries of the 1985 and 2017 earthquakes. She confirmed the drill would use the same seismic-alert tone as a real earthquake, broadcast via cellphone alerts and roughly 23,000 loudspeakers concentrated in Pacific-coast and central states. Separately, the director of Banobras presented the administration's public-private highway program of 19 projects, including extending Federal Highway 57 — which currently links Mexico City through Querétaro, San Luis Potosí and Saltillo — northward to the US border, financed without straining public finances. Sheinbaum also addressed a survey on foreign intervention in Mexico and a US report on drug trafficking, and discussed women's political participation.

events.title: Day 715 — Sheinbaum Leads Civic-Military Parade for 216th Independence Anniversary; 15,458 Troops, 99 Aircraft Fly Over Zócalo for First Time
events.detail: On September 16, 2026 (Day 715), President Sheinbaum, as commander-in-chief, led the civic-military parade marking the 216th anniversary of Mexican independence, reviewing the Armed Forces from the Zócalo before the terrestrial column advanced along the parade route to Campo Marte. The Army, Navy, Air Force and National Guard deployed 15,458 personnel, organized into six contingents — Justicia y Paz, Centinelas de la Nación, Crisol de Patriotas, Desarrollo Nacional, Fraternidad Solidaria and Raíces de Honor — alongside roughly 400 horses, 142 military working dogs and 26 eagles. For the first time in the parade's history, 99 aircraft flew simultaneously over the Plaza de la Constitución, including 45 tactical drones making their public debut, 5 Texan T-6C planes and 3 Naval Aviation MI-17 helicopters marking that branch's centennial; new SARAF Balam remote-fire-control armored vehicles and DN-XI units were also shown publicly for the first time. Sheinbaum used the occasion to again underscore Mexico's sovereignty and independence, days after the record-breaking Zócalo turnout at her September 15 Grito de Independencia address. No mañanera was held on September 15–16 for the Independence Day holiday; she was scheduled to resume the daily press conference on September 17.

events.title: Day 714 — Sheinbaum Gives Second Grito de Independencia Before Record 300,000-Strong Zócalo Crowd, Names Guadalupe Victoria and Antonia Nava
events.detail: On September 15, 2026 (Day 714), President Sheinbaum led the 216th-anniversary Grito de Independencia ceremony from the central balcony of the National Palace at 11:00 PM, ringing the historic bell and delivering 21 arengas before a Zócalo crowd Mexico City's interior affairs office put at more than 300,000 — surpassing the roughly 280,000 who attended her first Grito in 2025 and marking the biggest crowd yet for the ceremony. The roll call named traditional independence figures — Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, Josefa Ortiz Téllez-Girón, José María Morelos y Pavón, Leona Vicario, Vicente Guerrero and Gertrudis Bocanegra — alongside two names added for the first time this year, Guadalupe Victoria (Mexico's first president, 1824–1829) and insurgent Antonia Nava, while dropping Ignacio Allende and Manuela "La Capitana" Molina from the 2025 list. She also issued vivas recognizing Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples and, for the first time, Mexican migrants ("hermanos y hermanas migrantes"), fulfilling a pledge she made at her September 11 mañanera to "name new heroes and heroines that are not normally named." The ceremony came days after Sheinbaum told reporters, referencing ongoing USMCA tariff negotiations with Washington, "no vamos a firmar nada que tenga que ver con una afectación" to Mexico's sovereignty or economy. Free concerts by Grupo Intocable and Los Tigres del Norte preceded the ceremony, and the National Palace observed the bicentennial of Margarita Maza de Juárez, whom the federal government designated the honoree of the 2026 "Año de Margarita Maza" observance. No mañanera was held September 15–16 for the Independence Day holiday.

events.title: Day 713 — Sheinbaum Rejects Reports of US Military Personnel Entering Mexico as "Absurd," Cites 91% Poll Rejection of Intervention; Infonavit Chief Defends Assets
events.detail: On September 14, 2026 (Day 713, Monday), President Sheinbaum held her mañanera at the National Palace and dismissed media reports — which she said relied on "questionable sources" — that Mexico had approved US military personnel entering the country as "absurd," declaring "Mexico is not a piñata nor a matter for Americans" and reaffirming that national sovereignty is non-negotiable. She cited a survey showing 91% of respondents reject any US military intervention against 9% support, using the figures to counter claims circulating on social media. Separately, Infonavit director Octavio Romero Oropeza responded to a corruption and defamation campaign against him, stating his 2025 gross income (2.26 million pesos) was below the president's (2.30 million pesos), denying he owns luxury vehicles or jewelry, and noting properties he owns were acquired in 1984 and 1992, before his time in government; Infonavit officials also reported 4.856 million mortgage credits restructured, including 536,000 fully paid off and 4.32 million adjusted to more favorable terms. The Housing Secretary reported 667,000 homes under contract across 766 projects, with 89,000 additional homes assigned via Conavi and Infonavit. Sheinbaum also said she would ask the Legal Counsel whether artificial-intelligence regulation could be discussed during the ongoing 2026–27 electoral process, and announced there would be no mañanera on September 15–16 due to Independence Day celebrations.

events.title: Day 712 — Sheinbaum Leads 179th Niños Héroes Chapultepec Ceremony as Commander-in-Chief; Defense Secretary Pledges 'Absolute Loyalty'
events.detail: On September 13, 2026 (Day 712, Sunday), President Sheinbaum, in her capacity as commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces, led the ceremony marking the 179th anniversary of the 1847 defense of Chapultepec Castle against the U.S. invasion, held at the Altar a la Patria in the Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City, before members of Congress, federal officials, military commanders, cadets and students. Defense Secretary Ricardo Trevilla Trejo delivered the main address, calling to "strengthen our national unity, transmit to our children and youth the love for Mexico" and pledging that the Armed Forces would continue contributing to security and welfare "under your guidance," with "absolute loyalty" to Mexico and its institutions. A company of cadets from the Heroico Colegio Militar fired a rifle salute in memory of the six cadets who died defending the castle in 1847: Lieutenant Juan de la Barrera and cadets Juan Escutia, Agustín Melgar, Vicente Suárez, Fernando Montes de Oca and Francisco Márquez. Trevilla Trejo framed national sovereignty as both a constitutional mandate and a historical responsibility. Sheinbaum was scheduled to travel afterward to Pachuca, Hidalgo, to continue her "Honestidad y Resultados" report tour with a regional accountability event at the Domo de las Estrellas.

events.title: Day 711 — Sheinbaum Presents Yucatán Accountability Report in Mérida: 781,000 in Welfare Programs, Tren Maya Cargo Line, New Power Plant
events.detail: On September 12, 2026 (Day 711, Saturday), President Sheinbaum arrived in Mérida to deliver her regional "Honestidad y Resultados" (Honesty and Results) accountability report at the Yucatán Siglo XXI Convention Center, accompanied by Governor Joaquín "Huacho" Díaz Mena, federal cabinet officials and regional representatives. She reported that 781,215 Yucatecans receive benefits from federal welfare programs, representing an investment of more than 17 billion pesos in the state. On healthcare, she highlighted Yucatán's full integration into IMSS-Bienestar — guaranteeing free medical care — and the ongoing 5.41-billion-peso expansion of the Hospital General "Dr. Agustín O'Horán" in Mérida, plus construction of a Health University in Umán and three Benito Juárez García Welfare Universities. On infrastructure, she announced 244 new primary-care clinics for Yucatán as part of a 12,750-unit national network, cited the newly completed "Elvia Carrillo Puerto" combined-cycle power plant (454 million USD investment, 518 MW capacity, benefiting roughly 1.2 million residents), and detailed the first stage of the Tren Maya de Carga freight line — a 36.614-billion-peso investment with five cargo complexes and four operating yards. A new 1,100-student high school in Mérida was also announced. Yucatán was the 16th state visited in the tour's first two weeks; the "Honestidad y Resultados" tour reaches its midpoint here and is scheduled to conclude September 27 in Mexico City.

events.title: Day 710 — Sheinbaum Holds Mañanera in Chiapas, Cites Security Gains and Reversal of Forced Displacement; Questions INE Straight-Ballot Criteria
events.detail: On September 11, 2026 (Day 710, Friday), President Sheinbaum held her mañanera in Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas, alongside Governor Eduardo Ramírez Aguilar. Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch reported that since December 2024 the state has recorded 9,949 detentions, 1,832 recovered vehicles, 1,545 seized weapons and 71,798 confiscated cartridges, plus 18.6 tonnes of drugs secured through 101,907 joint interinstitutional operations, alongside a 64% drop in the daily average of intentional homicides and a 44% drop in other high-impact crimes compared to December 2024; the governor cited incorporating 800 experienced officers and a 55% police salary increase. Officials said forced displacement in Chiapas — which shifted in character from religious conflicts toward territorial disputes among criminal groups — has substantially reversed, with roughly 95% of displaced families returned home, including in Comalapa and Chicomuselo municipalities where residents had fled into Guatemala. On literacy, Chiapas reported reaching 194,818 people since 2025 against a 250,000 target. Sheinbaum also asked the INE to clarify new criteria that would count unfolded "straight ballots" as valid votes, and argued the agency's 2027 election budget should be based on 2024 spending adjusted for inflation. Asked about PAN officials' trip to Europe during the early stage of the 2026–27 electoral process, she said, "Tienen derecho... pero tiene su simbolismo," noting the timing near Mexico's Independence Day.

events.title: Day 709 — Economy Secretary Details Digital Economy Law, Sheinbaum Announces Zero VAT Rate for Books
events.detail: Also at the September 10, 2026 mañanera, the Secretariat of Economy detailed the Digital Economy Law for Digital and Electronic Payments — sent to the Chamber of Deputies alongside the 2027 Economic Package — which sets phased targets and timelines to shift public institutions, private companies and priority sectors from cash toward digital and electronic payment methods, with incentives and training tools aimed at helping micro and small businesses adopt secure electronic collection without hurting their income. Officials said more than 4.1 million taxpayers would benefit from simplified, fully digital tax procedures, including small businesses newly able to pay income tax on a quarterly rather than monthly basis. Separately, Sheinbaum announced books will be subject to a zero VAT rate rather than the standard exemption, allowing bookstores and publishers to recover VAT paid on their own expenses without the retail price to readers increasing.

events.title: Day 708 — Sheinbaum Presents 2027 Economic Package at National Palace, Announces Digital Economy Law to Curb Cash Use
events.detail: On September 9, 2026 (Day 708, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum presented the 2027 Economic Package at her mañanera in the National Palace, a day after Finance Secretary Édgar Amador Zamora formally delivered it to the Chamber of Deputies. Sheinbaum reiterated that the package "no contempla nuevos impuestos ni va a haber gasolinazos" (contemplates no new taxes and no fuel-price shocks), framing it as "responsible" and protective of welfare, health and education spending while pursuing gradual fiscal consolidation and reinforced anti-tax-evasion enforcement rather than new levies. She announced a new Digital Economy Law would be sent to Congress alongside the package, aimed at gradually reducing cash usage in commercial transactions through phased targets and timelines, promoting secure digital payment platforms, and providing incentives and training tools to help micro and small businesses adopt electronic collection methods without hurting their income. Sheinbaum said Finance Secretary Amador would detail the macroeconomic criteria, revenue initiatives and small-business support programs at her mañaneras on September 11 and 12. Officials confirmed the package projects total net spending of 10.636 trillion pesos, revenue of 9.157 trillion pesos, a deficit equal to 3.9% of GDP, and 2027 GDP growth of 1.5%–2.5%.

events.title: Day 707 — Hacienda Delivers 2027 Economic Package to Congress: 10.64 Trillion Pesos in Spending, Deficit Widens to 3.9% of GDP
events.detail: On September 8, 2026 (Day 707, Tuesday) at 6:00 PM, Finance Secretary Édgar Amador Zamora formally delivered the 2027 Economic Package (Paquete Económico) to the Chamber of Deputies, received by Chamber President Raúl Bolaños Cacho. The package — comprising the General Economic Policy Criteria, the Federal Revenue Law initiative, the Federal Expenditure Budget project and the Tax Miscellany — proposes total net spending of 10.636 trillion pesos against projected revenue of 9.157 trillion pesos, producing a budget deficit (Public Sector Financial Requirements) of 1.358 trillion pesos, equivalent to 3.9% of GDP — wider than the 3.5% figure previewed at Sheinbaum's September 3 mañanera, though Hacienda still frames it as "gradual" fiscal consolidation. Public debt is projected to rise to 55.8% of GDP in 2027 from 54.9% projected for 2026, attributed to higher debt-servicing costs and peso valuation effects on foreign-currency liabilities. Key macroeconomic assumptions: GDP growth of 1.5%–2.5% for 2027, year-end inflation of 3.0%, an average exchange rate near 18.0 pesos per dollar, a Mexican crude export mix price of $61.8/barrel, and oil production of 1.8 million barrels per day. Health spending is set at 1.1 trillion pesos (a 10%+ increase over 2026) and education at 1.3 trillion pesos, with social programs at 2.6% of GDP and infrastructure investment also at 2.6% of GDP; tax revenue is targeted at 15.4% of GDP, unchanged from 2026. Hacienda proposes income-tax law changes aimed at greater "fiscal equity" in business taxation plus additional anti-evasion and anti-false-invoicing measures, without raising existing tax rates. Separately, at her mañanera, Sheinbaum's Security Cabinet reported the national daily average of intentional homicides fell 53% comparing September 2024–August 2026, and Sheinbaum said fentanyl trafficking from Mexico to the U.S. has fallen more than 70%, a reduction she said U.S. authorities themselves recognize. She also defended the judicial reform, presenting data on reduced salaries, bonuses and benefits (including phone allowances) for the new Supreme Court justices — "still could lower it a bit there," she said, adding she pays her own cell phone bill — and said Mexico's decline on the 2025 PISA math exam was not unique to Mexico, while the OECD credited gains in science scores to the "Nueva Escuela Mexicana" curriculum.

events.title: Day 706 — Sheinbaum Calls Fox a 'Traitor to Democracy' Over Alito Moreno Meeting, Pledges No New Taxes in 2027 Economic Package
events.detail: On September 7, 2026 (Day 706, Monday), back at the National Palace after her ten-state Second Government Report tour, President Sheinbaum sharpened her earlier criticism of the September 4 meeting between former president Vicente Fox and PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno, mocking it as "the new vision of Mexican politics" and saying it would not go well for them. She called Fox a "traitor to democracy... seen by all Mexicans, first for the desafuero [2004 attempt to bar AMLO from the presidential race] and then for the 2006 electoral fraud," and accused PAN's younger leadership of ties to real-estate corruption scandals, arguing neither PRI nor PAN reaches double digits in support. Separately, ahead of the September 8 delivery of the 2027 Economic Package to Congress, Sheinbaum reiterated "no ha habido un aumento de impuestos ni va a haber" (there has not been a tax increase, nor will there be), saying additional revenue will come from combating tax evasion and shell companies used for false invoicing rather than new levies or new social programs, while keeping austerity in senior government salaries to fund existing welfare spending.

events.title: Day 705 — Sheinbaum Closes 10-State Report Tour in Monterrey and Saltillo, Touts Saltillo-Nuevo Laredo Train
events.detail: On September 6, 2026 (Day 705, Sunday), President Sheinbaum concluded the four-day, ten-state leg of her Second Government Report tour — which began September 3 in Morelos and Durango and passed through Zacatecas, San Luis Potosí, Aguascalientes, Colima, Jalisco and Nayarit — with stops in Nuevo León and Coahuila. At 10:30 AM she addressed a crowd of more than 10,000 at the Explanada de los Héroes in Monterrey alongside Governor Samuel García, highlighting health, infrastructure, housing and welfare gains in the state and announcing that construction on the Saltillo-Nuevo Laredo passenger rail line — a 396-kilometer project passing through Monterrey, already 3% complete — would receive its formal groundbreaking ("banderazo") in the coming days. At 1:15 PM in Saltillo, Coahuila's Parque Las Maravillas, she detailed a 985-kilometer rail corridor (3% built on the Saltillo-Nuevo Laredo segment), the Saltillo-Monclova highway modernization (158 km, 24% complete), the binational Puerto Verde logistics complex, and a 558-bed regional IMSS hospital under construction (10% complete) alongside new family-medicine units.

events.title: Day 704 — Sheinbaum Tours Colima, Jalisco and Nayarit; Rebuffs Cuyutlán Port Protesters, Blasts Fox-'Alito' Moreno Meeting
events.detail: On September 5, 2026 (Day 704, Saturday), President Sheinbaum continued her state-by-state Second Government Report tour with three stops in western Mexico: Colima (10:15 AM), the Arena VFG in Tlajomulco de Zúñiga, Jalisco (2:30 PM) and the Explanada de la Feria in Tepic, Nayarit (6:45 PM). In Colima, members of the Sal de Colima cooperative and other groups opposing the Port of Manzanillo's planned expansion into the Cuyutlán lagoon — a Ramsar wetland site — interrupted her remarks; Sheinbaum dismissed the disruption as provocation, saying, "Si fuera una demanda legítima, aceptarían reunirse con nosotros para atender sus inquietudes. No vamos a caer en la provocación." She reported 245,365 Colima residents receive Bienestar welfare programs and, in Jalisco, cited 962,111 beneficiaries of the Pension for Elderly Adults, alongside a confirmation that construction on the Mexico City-Querétaro-Irapuato-León-Guadalajara passenger rail line will begin in 2027. Separately, asked about the previous day's meeting between former president Vicente Fox and PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno at PRI headquarters, Sheinbaum said the pairing showed they "quieren regresar al pasado de corrupción y privilegios," framing it as an attempted PRI-PAN alliance ahead of the 2027 midterms and contrasting it with her government's welfare programs.

events.title: Day 703 — Security Cabinet Reports From Zacatecas: 200kg of Explosives in Ojocaliente Car Bomb, 3 Detained, CJNG-Cartel del Pacífico Dispute Cited
events.detail: On September 4, 2026 (Day 703, Friday), President Sheinbaum held her mañanera from Zacatecas — the first stop of a state-by-state tour following her Second Government Report — alongside Governor David Monreal and her federal Security Cabinet, delivering the findings promised after the August 30 Ojocaliente car bombing. Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said preliminary state-prosecutor analysis found the device used approximately 200 kilograms of explosive material, and confirmed three detentions: Juan Pedro "N" (apprehended August 31 for planting the device), plus Hipólito "N" and Miguel "N" (the latter already wanted on a separate homicide warrant), both linked to a criminal cell operating across Aguascalientes and Zacatecas. Harfuch identified a dispute between CJNG and Cartel del Pacífico cells over routes and territory as one of the main investigative lines, and said the case remains open, with the possibility that additional suspects are operating outside the state. He separately confirmed Mexico holds an active U.S. extradition detention order for Juan Carlos Valencia González ("El Pelón"), the CJNG's new leader following Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera's February 2026 death, noting Valencia González holds dual Mexican-American nationality — a detail that lands one day after Sheinbaum's dual-nationality candidacy ban was formally sent to Congress. On the broader security picture, García Harfuch reported 60,000 people arrested for high-impact crimes and 32,000 firearms seized (80% traced to the U.S.) since the administration began, and cited state-level figures showing Zacatecas's daily average of intentional homicides down 96% (from 4.5 in 2021 to 0.2 in 2026) and homicides overall down 85% since September 2024. The visit also included an economic and food-security readout: annual investment up 7.7% in June (public investment +10.9% YoY, private +6%), and record 2026-cycle production of 25.41 million tonnes of maize, 1.36 million tonnes of beans (+300,000 tonnes) and 14.4 billion liters of milk (+900 million liters).

events.title: Morena Federal Deputy Zenyazen Escobar García Found Dead in Veracruz; FGR Takes Over Investigation
events.detail: On the morning of September 4, 2026, federal deputy Zenyazen Roberto Escobar García (Morena, District 16, Córdoba, Veracruz) was found dead inside a vehicle on the Veracruz-Xalapa federal highway in the La Gloria community of Puente Nacional municipality, with at least one gunshot wound. Veracruz state government secretary Ricardo Ahued Bardahuil initially said authorities were not treating it as an attack, noting the vehicle showed no visible damage, while state prosecutors opened a homicide investigation; the Fiscalía General de la República (FGR) announced it would take over the case given Escobar's status as a sitting federal legislator. Escobar, 42, previously served as Veracruz's Secretary of Education (2018–2021) under Governor Cuitláhuac García and had drawn controversy in May 2026 over an altercation with a PRI legislator inside the Chamber of Deputies. Morena's Chamber coordinator Ricardo Monreal offered condolences, calling Escobar a public servant devoted to Veracruz; on September 8, Jucopo coordinators agreed not to form a special legislative commission, opting instead to await the FGR's forensic findings before any further chamber action, alongside a moment of silence and posthumous tribute.

events.title: Day 701 — Sheinbaum Unveils Redesigned Mañanera Stage, Breaking From AMLO-Era Set
events.detail: On September 2, 2026 (Day 701, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum resumed her morning press conference — now used for the "glosa" (line-by-line follow-up) of her Second Government Report — on a newly redesigned stage at the National Palace, the first change to "La Mañanera" set since López Obrador introduced the format in 2018. The old flat burgundy-and-white backdrop was replaced with three panels — two angled outward — forming a semi-curved space, still using burgundy, white and gray tones and retaining the "Conferencia de Prensa" screen. Reporters now sit noticeably closer to the podium than the roughly four-meter distance under the old layout; Sheinbaum remarked, "Ya los veo más cerca, antes casi no los veía." She said the redesign came from her presidential staff rather than any deliberate political signal.

events.title: Day 701 — Sheinbaum Calls Zacatecas Car Bombing "Isolated," Sends Security Cabinet Sept 5
events.detail: On September 2, 2026 (Day 701, Wednesday), asked about the August 30 car bomb attack outside the Ojocaliente, Zacatecas police command, President Sheinbaum called the incident "isolated" while acknowledging it was not the first such attack, and announced her Security Cabinet would travel to Zacatecas on Friday, September 5 to present findings on the criminal group responsible. She separately urged UNAM to consider opening additional undergraduate spaces and faculty positions after the university opened 2,000 new spots, and cited figures from Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde crediting the administration with 27 constitutional reforms and 76 secondary-law reforms since October 2024. Sheinbaum also praised customs and tax authorities for a fuel-theft crackdown, citing the arrest of Fernando Farías Laguna as helping curb contraband and stabilize gasoline prices, and rejected suggestions of a rift with Morena Senate leader Adán Augusto López, saying their direct contact had lessened but coordination with other party leaders continued.

events.title: Day 700 — Sheinbaum Delivers Second Government Report From National Palace, Cites 51% Homicide Drop and Sovereignty Message
events.detail: On September 1, 2026 (Day 700, Tuesday), President Claudia Sheinbaum delivered her Second Government Report ("En Defensa de la Soberanía"-style annual address) from the National Palace at 11:00 AM CDMX time, replacing that day's regular mañanera. Headline claims: intentional homicides down 51% since the administration's October 2024 start (about 44 fewer deaths per day) and high-impact crimes down 32%; the monthly minimum wage risen from 2,800 pesos (2018) to 9,584 pesos, with labor poverty at its lowest level since 2005; annual inflation at 3.12% (July 2026) on a downward trend; the peso trading near 17/USD; roughly 60 million people employed and unemployment at 2.7%; H1 2026 foreign direct investment of approximately $34.97 billion (+2.1% YoY); GDP growth revised to 1.4% QoQ / 1.9% YoY for Q2 2026; and a new welfare push toward 42.86 million beneficiaries by year-end backed by roughly 1 trillion pesos in social spending. On security, the government cited 63,000 people detained for crimes since October 2024, 207 priority targets arrested, 32,824 firearms seized, 519 tonnes of drugs seized and 2,725 clandestine labs dismantled. Health and infrastructure figures included 33 new hospitals, 23+ million "Salud Casa por Casa" home visits, Tren Maya ridership of 2.5 million passengers, and a Pemex financial-debt reduction of roughly $20 billion. Sheinbaum highlighted a new indigenous-rights law and framed welfare programs as "turning love into public policy." She struck a conciliatory, unity-focused tone toward Morena ahead of the 2027 midterms — "que nadie se equivoque: aquí no hay divisiones, aquí no hay rompimientos" — while repeating her sovereignty line that international cooperation "no significa sumisión" and that Mexico's sovereignty "no se negocia, no se entrega y no se comparte." Opposition reaction was sharp: PAN deputy Federico Döring presented a rival "informe real" citing low growth, rising debt, Pemex's financial crisis, insecurity and disappearances; PAN also noted her administration's 0.8% average growth trails AMLO's 1.1%. PRI national leader Alejandro Moreno accused Morena of degrading quality of life and shielding drug traffickers.

events.title: Car Bomb Explodes Outside Police Headquarters in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas — 11 Injured
events.detail: On August 30, 2026 (Sunday) around 7:30 PM local time, an unidentified man parked a vehicle laden with explosives in front of the municipal police (DSPM) command in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas, then fled on foot; the device detonated when an officer approached to inspect it. Eleven people were injured, including civilians and municipal police, at least two seriously. The blast damaged roughly five city blocks — at least seven homes, businesses, private vehicles and patrol units, with windows shattered throughout the area. State Security Secretary Arturo Medina Mayoral said authorities were investigating possible involvement of a Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) cell; the vehicle used had been reported stolen in Jalisco since April, and the explosive materials resembled those used in mining operations. A near-simultaneous explosion in Villa García led to the detention of an 18-year-old who claimed CJNG membership. State officials said the attack was the 17th documented explosive-device attack on security forces in Zacatecas over the prior two years and the 10th of 2026 alone, part of an escalating wave that has included motorcycle-borne devices and improvised metal-pipe bombs ("niples"). State and federal forces reinforced the area following the blast.

events.title: Fed Raises Interest Rates to 3.75%–4.00%, First Hike in Over Three Years
events.detail: The Federal Reserve on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, raised its benchmark federal funds rate by a quarter point to a range of 3.75%–4.00% — the first rate hike since July 2023 and a reversal from new Chair Kevin Warsh's prior holds. The FOMC voted unanimously, citing persistently elevated inflation driven in large part by soaring fuel prices tied to the ongoing US-Israel war with Iran, which has pushed oil prices higher and broadened price pressures across the economy. Updated Fed projections point to one additional rate increase before year-end, with rates expected to hold steady through 2027. The hike raises borrowing costs for mortgages, auto loans and credit cards just as Trump campaigns on economic performance ahead of the November midterms, and comes days after a Fox News poll found 63% of voters say his administration has made the economy worse.

events.title: CBO: Iran War Has Cost $38.1 Billion, Is Driving Up Inflation and Borrowing Costs
events.detail: The Congressional Budget Office released a report Tuesday, September 15, 2026, finding the US-Israel war with Iran, launched February 28, has directly cost the United States $38.1 billion through August 1 and continues to cost roughly $2-3 billion per month, with more than half the total ($21.7 billion) spent replacing munitions — including $13.1 billion in missile-defense interceptors CBO estimates will take five years for the Pentagon to fully replace. CBO attributed more than 40% of US inflation during the second quarter of 2026 to the war and projected it will add roughly half a percentage point to inflation in the first quarter of 2027, also pushing up borrowing costs; the report noted the average 30-year mortgage rate, under 6% before the war began, stood at 7.22% on the day of the report. The findings add a nonpartisan cost estimate to a war Trump has repeatedly predicted will end 'right after the midterms, maybe before,' and follow the administration's own August acknowledgment that it is 'not in a hurry' to resume talks with Tehran.

events.title: Canadians Adjust to Sustained Impact of Trump's Trade War
events.detail: Canadians describe how they are adjusting economically and politically to the sustained impact of Trump's trade war, including supply chain shifts and consumer price pressures as tariff policies continue to reshape North American commerce.

events.title: Trump Promises $5,000 'Dividend' Checks to Every American Adult if Republicans Keep Congress
events.detail: Closing out the RNC's first-ever midterm convention at Dallas's American Airlines Center on Thursday, September 10, 2026, President Trump pledged that every American adult citizen would receive a $5,000 check — which he dubbed the 'Trump dividend' — if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in November. 'If the Republicans win, you win with us and you get $5,000,' Trump told the crowd, offering no detail on funding mechanics, though Vice President Vance had indicated tariff revenue would partly cover the cost. With roughly 245 million US adult citizens, the payout would total an estimated $1.2 trillion. Tax Foundation economist Erica York said the checks would 'spend almost all the revenue that the new tariffs are projected to bring in over a decade,' and former IMF chief economist Kenneth Rogoff warned it would 'blow up' an already unsustainable deficit; election-law scholar Rick Hasen said Trump likely has First Amendment latitude to make the campaign promise (citing Brown v. Hartlage) but actual payments would require congressional approval. Similar Trump pledges in 2025 — a tariff dividend and a DOGE dividend — never materialized. In the same speech Trump also vowed to make his tax cuts permanent, pursue 'most-favored-nation' prescription drug pricing, redirect health-insurer payments directly to citizens, and told the crowd 'you go to hell' if they don't vote in November.

events.title: Treasury Sanctions 27 Iranian Airlines Under 'Operation Economic Outcast'
events.detail: The Treasury Department sanctioned 36 targets on Tuesday, September 8, 2026 — including 27 of Iran's remaining commercial airlines, aircraft-procurement front companies, and cargo service providers — under Executive Order 13902 as part of Secretary Scott Bessent's 'Operation Economic Outcast' campaign, first unveiled in August. The action targeted Mahan Air (first designated in 2011) and newer carriers including Varesh Airlines, Sepehran Airlines, and Qeshm Air, several of which still fly to Dubai, Muscat, and Kuwait City. Bessent said: 'Let this be a warning to anyone doing business with Iran's remaining airlines, all of which we sanctioned today: You are at risk of being cut off from the global financial system.' FinCEN separately alerted US banks to increase scrutiny of transactions linked to Iranian aviation procurement, the latest step in the financial-pressure campaign the administration has pursued since the Aug 24 'economic D-Day' sanctions round.

events.title: Trump Escalates Canada Trade War: Bans Canadian Dairy, Alcohol and Motorcycle Imports Under Section 338
events.detail: President Trump signed five proclamations Tuesday, September 8, 2026, sharply escalating the trade war with Canada in direct response to Canada's retaliatory tariffs that took effect at 12:01 a.m. the same day. Three proclamations impose outright bans, effective September 29, 2026, on imports of Canadian dairy products, molasses and non-alcoholic beer, most alcoholic beverages, and motorcycles; two others revise the 50% Section 338 tariff list, removing cement, road salt and hospital pads while adding all-terrain vehicles, additional cheeses and motorboats. Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 — unused for nearly a century before Trump invoked it in late August 2026 — lets the president act without a new statute. USTR Jamieson Greer said of Canada's retaliation, 'That's not the kind of company you really want to be running in.' Earlier the same day, Trump posted on Truth Social that he would bar federal agencies from buying Canadian goods 'unless Canada restores full and fair reciprocity for American Farmers and Companies.'

events.title: US Imposes New 10% Section 301 Tariff on Mexico Over Forced-Labor Import Enforcement Gaps
events.detail: The Office of the US Trade Representative announced the results of a Section 301 forced-labor investigation covering 60 economies, imposing new ad valorem tariffs effective July 24–25, 2026. Mexico was placed in the more favorable 10% tier (rather than the 12.5% tier applied to countries with no forced-labor import prohibition at all) because USTR determined it has import bans on the books but has failed to effectively enforce them against goods transiting its supply chains. Crucially, Mexican goods that qualify for duty-free treatment under USMCA rules of origin remain exempt from the new tariff, so the measure primarily affects the roughly 11-16% of Mexico-US trade that does not claim USMCA preference. The action landed in the middle of the ongoing USMCA joint-review negotiations and added a new friction point alongside earlier tariff threats on autos, steel, aluminum, and copper.

events.title: Trump Threatens 30% Reciprocal Tariff on Mexico Starting August 1
events.detail: President Trump announced that reciprocal tariffs on Mexican goods would rise to 30% effective August 1, 2026, escalating pressure during the ongoing USMCA joint review process. The threat came roughly two weeks after the US declined to renew USMCA on its current 16-year terms at the July 1 joint review, and as bilateral negotiating rounds on automotive rules of origin, steel, and aluminum continued. As of mid-July, USMCA-qualifying goods (an estimated 89% of Mexico-US trade) continued to enter under the existing 0% preferential rate, with the 30% threat aimed at non-qualifying goods and intended as leverage ahead of the next negotiating round scheduled for the week of July 20.

events.title: Banxico Holds Benchmark Rate at 6.5% in Unanimous Vote, Signals End of Easing Cycle
events.detail: The Bank of Mexico's governing board unanimously voted to hold its benchmark interest rate at 6.5% at its June 25, 2026 meeting, confirming the two-year easing cycle that began in March 2024 has concluded. Headline inflation continued to ease, falling from 4.45% in April to 3.55% by mid-June, within Banxico's target tolerance range. Policymakers signaled they will likely keep the rate at this level going forward, citing upside risks from trade disruptions tied to the ongoing USMCA review, geopolitical tensions, persistent core inflation, and possible peso depreciation.

events.title: Banxico Cuts Benchmark Rate to 6.5% in Split Vote, Signals End of Two-Year Easing Cycle
events.detail: Mexico's central bank (Banco de México / Banxico) voted 3-2 to cut its benchmark overnight interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.5% — the lowest level since May 2022 — following April inflation data showing a first deceleration since December 2025. The governing board simultaneously signaled this cut marked the end of a two-year-plus easing cycle that had lowered rates from the August 2023 peak of 11.25%. Board members in the minority voted to hold rates, citing continued uncertainty over US tariff impacts on inflation and peso stability. The peso traded at approximately 17.31 per dollar in early May, representing significant strengthening from the 2025 average of approximately 19.20. The rate decision comes against a complex macroeconomic backdrop: while inflation is moderating and the peso has strengthened, Mexico's economy contracted in Q1 2026 (largest decline in over a year) with investment falling 6.6% in 2025. The Banxico decision was interpreted as a signal that monetary policy has done its work and that structural reforms — fiscal stimulus, investment promotion through Plan México Acciones — must now carry the weight of economic revival. The 6.5% rate still provides meaningful real interest rates above the approximately 4% headline inflation reading, preserving Mexico's financial stability credentials.

events.title: Mexico's Labor Poverty Rate Hits Historic Low at 32.3% in Q4 2025, Despite GDP Contraction Warnings
events.detail: Mexico's Labor Ministry (STPS) and CONEVAL released Q4 2025 labor poverty data on May 6, 2026, confirming a historic milestone: the share of Mexicans in households unable to cover basic food needs with wage income fell to 32.3% — the lowest on record since the measure was introduced. Labor Minister Marath Bolaños highlighted the figure as evidence that the minimum wage increases (cumulative 283% since 2018 under AMLO and Sheinbaum) have translated into genuine material gains for low-income workers. Mexico raised the minimum wage again in January 2026 to MX$278.80/day (approximately $16.10/day), the highest nominal level since the modern wage was established. However, the milestone came amid contradictory signals: the Q1 2026 GDP contraction of 0.8% — confirmed by INEGI on April 30 — created downside risk for formal employment in the near term. Bloomberg's May 6 analysis argued that 'Mexico will lose more from a bad USMCA rewrite than from no deal,' noting that the agreement generates approximately $839 billion in annual bilateral trade and sustains millions of formal jobs in manufacturing, agriculture, and services. The labor poverty reduction is credited to formal job creation driven by nearshoring investment — FDI into Mexico's manufacturing sector hit $36.9 billion in 2024, the highest on record — and the sustained minimum wage policy. Critics noted that 32.3% labor poverty still means nearly one in three Mexicans cannot cover basic food needs through labor income alone.

events.title: Mexico's Sovereign Infrastructure Fund (MIP) Seeks to Deploy $12 Billion; World Cup Airspace Security Decree Published
events.detail: Mexico's sovereign infrastructure fund (Fondo Mexicano del Petróleo para la Estabilización y el Desarrollo, MIP) announced it is actively seeking to deploy USD $12 billion in new infrastructure investments — a major complement to the Plan México Acciones framework unveiled the previous day. The deployment targets strategic infrastructure including ports, rail corridors, industrial parks, and energy grid upgrades to support the nearshoring manufacturing boom. Separately, on May 5, Mexico's Secretariat of National Defense (SEDENA) published a formal decree establishing four Zones of Surveillance and Protection of Mexican Airspace (ZVP) for the FIFA World Cup period running from May 11 through July 20, 2026 — covering Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Monterrey. The decree operationalizes Mexico's counter-drone (CUAS) commitments and coordinates military airspace control with civilian aviation authorities. Mexico City's Benito Juárez Airport simultaneously completed three-day tactical exercises simulating hijacking, hostage-taking, and CBRN (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear) scenarios. The dual announcements — major investment mobilization and World Cup security finalization — reflected the Sheinbaum government's effort to project institutional capacity despite the Sinaloa governor crisis and US sovereignty disputes of the preceding week.

events.title: Sheinbaum Unveils Plan México Acciones: MX$5.6 Trillion Infrastructure Push to Revive Contracting Economy
events.detail: President Claudia Sheinbaum unveiled 'Plan México Acciones,' an expanded investment framework designed to reverse Mexico's economic contraction after Q1 2026 posted the country's largest GDP decline in over a year. The plan encompasses a MX$5.6 trillion (approximately USD $407 billion) public-private infrastructure investment pipeline for 2026–2030, immediate accelerated tax deductions of 41–91% on new fixed-asset investments, and a unified digital foreign trade platform to reduce bureaucratic friction for exporters. Mexico's sovereign infrastructure fund (MIP) separately announced plans to deploy USD $12 billion in new infrastructure projects. The plan directly responds to a 2025 investment contraction of 6.6% — driven by investor uncertainty over the judicial reform, USMCA tariff tensions, and security concerns. Sheinbaum framed the initiative as Mexico's response to the nearshoring opportunity, with dozens of Asian and US manufacturing companies seeking to relocate supply chains from China to Mexico. The plan attracted cautious interest from the private sector, though business associations noted that judicial certainty and rule-of-law improvements — not tax incentives alone — were the primary investment constraints. Bloomberg noted the initiative came as Mexico sought to project economic confidence ahead of the May 25 USMCA formal review round.
